text: {"answerable": true, "answer": "SchNet uses a shifted softplus, ssp(x) = ln(0.5e^x + 0.5), as its non-linearity throughout the network. The shift ensures ssp(0) = 0 and improves convergence [W2726670313#010][W2778051509#006]. It matters for force fields because SchNet's forces are obtained by differentiating the energy with respect to atom positions, so the model must be at least twice differentiable to allow gradient descent on the force loss [W2726670313#010]. The function has infinite order of continuity, which gives smooth potential energy surfaces, force fields, and second derivatives [W2778051509#006]. By contrast, the passages note that ReLU-type activations are excluded for this reason, because non-smooth activations cause discontinuities in the forces [W3093149769#039]."}
